_comment: The canonical stat vocabulary. Every system that hands CharacterSystem a stat modifier — base_bonuses tables in perks.json, perk effects, spell effects, traits, items — names its stats from here. Before this file existed there was no shared vocabulary: perks.json wrote `attack`, `movement_speed` and `strength_weapon_damage` while update_derived_stats read `accuracy`, `movement` and `damage`, so 28 of the 40 base_bonuses keys landed nowhere and the 12 that landed were read as flat points when the data means percentages.
_comment_mode: `mode` says how a modifier combines.  scaling: the value is a percentage of the stat's computed base, so 130 means +130% and the base must exist for it to mean anything.  rate: the stat has no base and the percentage IS the value, accumulating additively (a 15% shop discount).  flat: the value is added as-is (a companion, a die-roll bonus).
_comment_pct_base: A scaling stat whose real base can legitimately be zero — accuracy is a pure bonus on top of a flat 80% hit chance — declares `pct_base`, the notional base its percentage is taken against. Only accuracy needs one. Armor deliberately does not: an unarmoured character gaining armor from the Armor skill would be wrong.

armor.description: Flat damage reduction from worn armor.

armor_pierce.description: Armor ignored by this character's attacks.

accuracy.description: Percentage points added to the 80% base hit chance.

dodge.description: Percentage points subtracted from an attacker's hit chance.

spellpower.description: Scales spell damage, healing and duration.

magic_damage_reduction_pct.description: Percent of incoming magic damage ignored.

mental_resistance_pct.description: Resistance to fear, charm and confusion.

mana_cost_pct.description: Percent change to the mana cost of spells this character casts. Negative is cheaper — the data writes a reduction as a negative number, so the sign is kept rather than inverted into a "reduction" that would read backwards.

healing_pct.description: Percent bonus to healing this character performs.

burning_damage_pct.description: Percent bonus to Burning damage this character inflicts.

status_effect_chance_pct.description: Percent bonus to the chance a status this character applies lands.

stun_chance_pct.description: Percent chance a hit also stuns.

effect_duration_pct.description: Percent bonus to the duration of buffs and debuffs this character applies.

summon_hp_pct.description: Percent bonus to the HP of creatures this character summons.

loot_chance_pct.description: Percent bonus to the chance loot drops at all.

buy_discount_pct.description: Percent off shop prices when buying.

sell_markup_pct.description: Percent added to shop prices when selling.

trading_price_pct.description: Percent improvement to prices in both directions.

charm_effectiveness_pct.description: Percent bonus to social and persuasion outcomes.

social_roll_success_pct.description: Percent bonus to social roll success.

morale_effects_pct.description: Percent bonus to the strength of morale effects this character causes.

luck_modifier_pct.description: Percent bonus applied to luck-based rolls.

consumable_power_pct.description: Percent bonus to the effect of consumables this character uses.

crafting_quality_pct.description: Percent bonus to the quality of crafted items.

crafting_yield_pct.description: Percent bonus to the quantity produced when crafting.

travel_speed_pct.description: Percent bonus to overworld travel speed.

supply_duration_pct.description: Percent bonus to how long party supplies last.

max_companions.description: Additional companions the party may hold.

party_skill_checks.description: Flat bonus added to party-wide skill check rolls.

temp_hp.description: Temporary hit points, absorbed before real HP.

_comment_aliases: Legacy spellings, kept so existing data keeps working. Resolve every incoming stat name through these before use. The list may shrink as data is rewritten; it should not grow.
